policies.title: CA-4 Category A ordinary passports: visa-free Honduras entry
policies.summary: The current COCESNA CA-4 eAIP defines Category A as visa-exempt for ordinary passports travelling to Honduras. This policy includes the current listed Category A passports after applying directly stated Honduras-specific changes for Bolivia, Ecuador, Latvia, Taiwan and the United Kingdom.
conditions: Applies only to ordinary passports in the stated CA-4 Category A baseline; it does not flatten diplomatic, official, service, residence, refugee, stateless, provisional or special-document treatment.

The current CA-4 schedule expressly records Honduras-specific deviations: Bolivia and Ecuador receive Category A treatment, while Latvia receives Category B treatment. Taiwan is in the listed Category A cohort.

A tourist normally receives up to 90 days at entry and may seek a 30-day extension. Passport, onward or continuing ticket, migration form, funds, purpose, lodging, health and individual-admissibility requirements apply.
CA-4 residence, qualifying third-country visa or residence and other special exceptions are conditional and do not replace this nationality baseline.

policies.title: CA-4 Category B/C ordinary passports: advance Honduran visa required
policies.summary: The current CA-4 eAIP places these ordinary passports in Category B (consular) or C (consulted). Both require advance visa processing for the unconditional ordinary-passport baseline, so both normalize to visa_required rather than eVisa, ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: Category B is an advance consular visa: INM says it is affixed to the passport and delivered at the personal, in-person appointment. Category C requires prior written INM validation before the applicant proceeds at a Honduran consulate.
The Category B/C grouping is only a normalized outcome; it does not erase the consulted-visa authorization, sponsor, documentary, fee, purpose or consular requirements that vary by category.

The current schedule's Honduras observations place Latvia and the Dominican Republic in Category B. The current eAIP places Jordan in Category C; this candidate does not use the unavailable SRE circular to classify the United Kingdom or Palestinian rows.

A Category B visitor with a qualifying United States, Canadian or Exchange visa, or qualifying Category-A-country residence, may receive Category A treatment; a Category C visitor with stated qualifying documents may be reduced only to Category B. These are conditional document exceptions, not nationality baselines.

CA-4 residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, emergency, refugee, stateless and special-document cases remain outside this ordinary-passport visitor classification. Final admission remains with migration authorities.
